title: A LAND FLOWING WITH MILK AND HONEY

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Today, in the month of Aviv, you are leaving. When the LORD brings you into the
land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Hivites and Jebusites-the land he
swore to your ancestors to give you, a land flowing with milk and honey-you are
to observe this ceremony in this month." - Ex 13:4-5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
On the very first day of the journey, God speaks about the destination.

They are standing in the desert with nothing, and He describes a land flowing
with milk and honey. He even names the nations currently living there, so there
is no illusion that it will be easy. But the promise is fixed, because it rests
on an oath God swore to their ancestors, not on Israel's strength.

This is God's kindness. He gives His people a picture of the end at the very
start of the hard part. Not to spare them the wilderness, but to sustain them
through it.

We should be careful here. This land promise was given to Israel specifically,
and it is not a guarantee that Christians will receive comfortable
circumstances. Prosperity teaching goes badly wrong at exactly this point. But
the character of God behind the promise has not changed. He still tells His
people how the story ends, and He still keeps His word.

For believers, the destination is described differently: "a better country, a
heavenly one" (Heb 11:16). Paul kept going through beatings and shipwreck
because he had seen the end.

Knowing the destination is what makes the desert bearable.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When did you last think seriously about where you are ultimately headed?
2. How would today feel different if the end were more real to you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that You have told me how the story ends. Let that hope carry
me through the difficult stretch I am in now. Amen.
